1.e4 c5 2.c3 d5 3.exd5 Qxd5 4.d4 cxd4 5..strategy: Defends the d4 pawn with a developing move and leaves the b1 knight free to come to c3 with a gain of time on the queen. White accepts the isolated pawn and plays for active pieces.
Develops the bishop outside the pawn chain with a pin on the knight, which defends d4. Black then piles up on the d4 pawn, and White has to meet that pressure with accurate development.
1.e4 c5 2.c3 d5 3.exd5 Qxd5 4.d4 cxd4 5..name: Sicilian Defence: Alapin Variation, Barmen Defence, Central Exchange

1.e4 c5 2.c3 d5 3.exd5 Qxd5 4.d4 cxd4 5..strategy: Strikes at d4 with a pawn, adding a third attacker, and opens lines for Black's pieces. It is the riskier way to fight for the centre: the pawn structure loosens and the queen on d5 can be hit once the d-file opens, so Black has to be sure the activity is worth it.
